apps.description: The Academy's maintained build of KisMac: passive Wi-Fi scanning, hidden-SSID detection, client mapping, and GPS/KML export, remediated and rebuilt for macOS High Sierra. For network education and authorized testing of your own networks only. Installs as KisMac2.app under the Academy's own bundle identity (com.detroitautomationacademy.kismac) and carries the Academy audit entry. The bundle identity changed from the upstream com.igrsoft.kismac in this build, so the first launch is a fresh profile — preferences, Keychain items, and saved state do not carry over. It installs side by side with the Workbench entry (Workbench.app). Its app icon is the Academy re-cut under the amended SDS-3 construction (ink silhouette on the white tile) — the upstream color art no longer ships in the build.

apps.buildNotes: Handler-rank build (MD-T5, Distro files/24): the Markdown document type now declares LSHandlerRank Alternate — MacDown presents itself as an alternate handler for markdown, deliberately not the system default and not the owner. Routing from Muse (Academy Build) opens files in MacDown explicitly; any system-default change is the owner's consented act in Muse, never something MacDown claims by installing. The plain-text and catch-all document entries are unchanged and carry no rank. Everything else stands from the SDS-10 conformance build: SDS-8 welcome screen (MPWelcomeController), SDS-10 conformance entry, Academy audit entry, Academy bundle ID, trimmed monochrome icon.

apps.description:
Distro is the Detroit Automation Academy's native application-store app for macOS High Sierra: it browses the Academy catalog, downloads Academy-maintained apps from the AutomatedTechnologies GitHub org, verifies every download by SHA-256 before install, and carries no privileged helper. Prepared at DAADV3 T1 codification (2026-11-07); not yet published — publication remains gated on Distro tranche D-T5. Disassembled. Scanned. Recompiled. Distro distributes only apps carrying the Academy audit entry in their plist — proof of the Academy pipeline. distro-test-17 applies the SDS-9 liquid-glass cues to the store chrome: layered tint depth, the glass hairline pair on the dividers and sheet edges, capsule state controls, and the status word in a capsule chip — flat tints only, no behavior change.

© 2026 Detroit Automation Academy / Automated Technologies. All rights reserved. Detroit Automation Academy, Automated Technologies, Distro, Workbench, Live Transit Detroit, The Signal, and the Academy monochrome logo are marks of the Academy, used under the founder's permission. Academy-original works are licensed under the Academy License (revocable); upstream open-source components remain under their own licenses. distro-test-22 adds Update All: when updates are pending, one button runs them sequentially — each app still verified by SHA-256 and the audit gate on its own — and ends with a single summary. The detail pane now shows build notes for the catalog version and the installed app's file path. Catalog fetches now bypass HTTP caches, so Refresh always returns the current catalog.
apps.name: Distro
apps.tagline: The Academy's application store for High Sierra — browse, install, and update Academy apps.
apps.buildNotes: Pre-flight installs (charter section 6): before Distro places an update, it closes the app if it is running — politely first, force-quit only if the app does not quit, and the install stops untouched if the app still will not quit — and removes the previous version's bundle. Your app data is stored separately from the bundle and is never deleted or moved by an install, so settings and history carry across every update. An app that replaced an earlier product under a different name can declare its predecessor identities, and pre-flight treats a running predecessor and its bundle the same way. Everything else stands: SHA-256 verification and the audit gate in DistroInstaller still run before pre-flight, so an unverified download never disturbs a running app; the unified registered logo, the version read from the bundle on the welcome screen, the functional menu bar, and academy-distro:// deep links all carry over.

apps.description: Minion is the Academy's build of the open-source muse-desktop client (MIT, v0.3.0) on Electron 22.3.27 — the last Electron that runs on macOS 10.13 — so Intel High Sierra machines can run a Muse client at all; the official Muse app requires Apple Silicon and a current macOS. It is the renamed successor of Muse (Academy Build): its declared predecessor is Muse (Academy Build), bundle ai.muse.desktop, which an install of Minion supersedes. The owner renamed it Minion on 2026-11-10, and it ships under the Academy bundle identity com.detroitautomationacademy.minion (the earlier upstream-ID carve-out was revoked the same evening: nothing lists without a disassembly and rebuild). Its icon is Minion's registered mark — the scheming side-eye dog — cut to the SDS-3 construction: white tile and ink artwork, no black field, fully monochrome. App data is stored separately, outside the bundle, at ~/Library/Application Support/com.detroitautomationacademy.minion; the previous version's data stays untouched under its own location. Version 0.4.0 adds the Academy feature layer: repaired window management (no window opens partially off-screen; your window arrangement is restored), up-arrow sent-message history in the message box, markdown downloads that open in MacDown with a consented system-default offer, and a genuine Terminal view (View menu, Command-T): the app's own terminal window over the live hosted session. The earlier stylesheet Terminal Skin was rejected by the owner and is deleted outright. Unofficial build: not a Meta product and not endorsed by Meta. Unsigned test build.
apps.name: Minion
apps.tagline: The Academy's Muse client for High Sierra — Minion, under its own name and mark.
apps.buildNotes: Minion — the renamed successor of Muse (Academy Build). PREDECESSOR: Minion replaces Muse (Academy Build), bundle ai.muse.desktop — that is the previous version an install of Minion supersedes. App data is stored separately: Minion keeps no user data inside the app bundle; its data lives at ~/Library/Application Support/com.detroitautomationacademy.minion, a fresh location under the new bundle identity. The previous version's data remains untouched at ~/Library/Application Support/Muse, and removing either version's bundle never touches either data store — expect a fresh sign-in and a fresh start in Minion; nothing is migrated. The icon is Minion's own mark: the scheming side-eye dog, rendered to the Academy monochrome standard (white tile, ink artwork, no black field). Everything else stands from the previous builds: the genuine Terminal view (View menu, Command-T) over the live hosted session, markdown routing to MacDown with the consented system default, window repair, up-arrow message history (kept in Minion's own data store), the SDS-8 welcome. Unsigned test build; the runtime verdict is the owner's, at the Air sitting.

apps.description: An Academy-original utility for a USB-connected AirPods Max (Lightning generation) that will not respond. Five-section diagnostics — USB enumeration and power, IORegistry device node, CoreAudio device list, Bluetooth pairing and link, recent bluetoothd/coreaudiod log evidence — with a branching verdict; guided Restart and Factory Reset sheets for the headphones (including the 15-second reset hold timer); a Restart Services action for coreaudiod and bluetoothd; and a Firmware panel that reads the device firmware and compares it with the latest for this model (6F25, Apple Support 106340), evaluating Apple's automatic-update conditions live. Installs as AirPodsMaxDiag.app under its own Academy bundle identity (com.detroitautomationacademy.airpodsmaxdiag) and carries the Academy audit entry. AirPods Max is a trademark of Apple Inc.; this utility is not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.
apps.name: AirPods Max Diagnostics
apps.tagline: Diagnose and recover a non-responsive AirPods Max (Lightning) — USB, Bluetooth, audio, firmware.
apps.buildNotes: Defect fix: the app shipped with no menu bar — the programmatic UI never built a main menu (no nib, and no code called setMainMenu:). The main menu is now constructed in code and installed at launch: app menu (About, Quit), File (Save Report…, Close Window), Edit (standard editing for the report view), Diagnostics (the window's nine actions, on the menu bar), Window, Help. No diagnostic behavior changes. Runtime verification at the owner's Air sitting, evening of 2026-11-10.
